# Barrel generation

Read when a package's generated `src/index.ts` barrel, its answer from `readExportsGeneration`, the generator behind them, or a module's place under `src/internal/` is in question. `SKILL.md` says only that the build generates barrels; this page is how, and why generation is unguarded.

## Barrels are generated by the build, not in front of it

A package's root entry has one name by kind: `src/index.ts` for a library, and `src/module.ts` for a Nuxt module, which Nuxt loads by its own convention. A Nuxt module is the package that depends on `@nuxt/kit`. `scripts/src/workspace/entryNames.test.ts` holds every package's `.` source arm to that name, and the package generator writes the same names, so a library's manifest points at the barrel its build writes rather than at a module beside it.

tsdown bundles from `src/index.ts` and never writes it — its default entry only checks the file exists. A library normally commits a hand-written barrel as its chosen public API; here the file is generated and gitignored instead, and the generator is ours. Every module with an export outside `src/internal/` is public (`.agents/skills/file-organization/SKILL.md`, "One function per file, exported or not"), and the Settled line below is the one rule that keeps a module private.

`getTsdownConfiguration` runs `generateBarrels` from a `build:prepare` hook, so no manifest repeats the command. What a package generates is read off the package by `readExportsGeneration`, a member of the value set `ExportsGeneration`: `Vue` when the package ships `.vue` files, `TypeScript` when its `.` export names its `src/index.ts`, and `None` otherwise, so no barrel is generated (a Nuxt module's `.` export names its `src/module.ts`, and `shared-node` names its own entrypoints with no `.` export). No build option states it beside the package, so the answer is one function, and the create's barrel phase calls the same `generateBarrels` (`scripts/src/services/worktree/create/writeWorktreeBarrels.ts`). `generateBarrels` also hands `generateExports` the subpath exclusions `getSubpathExclusions` derives from the `source` arms of the package's own `package.json`, so the root barrel leaves out every subpath's module (see "A subpath is a hand-written barrel"). A package that loads some directories through `import()` names them in the call it makes from a `build:prepare` hook of its own, `generateBarrels(cwd, [...])`, which replaces the base's and adds them to the derived exclusions (genshin-world's kit, avatar and card-game modules, and the directories nothing in the repo imports from its barrel). The source barrel and the component barrel leave every path handed in out, a folder or a module, so the entry does not load them. There is no separate command: a package's build is the regeneration, and cheap enough to be the only one. The create's phase passes no folders of its own, so a barrel it writes for a package with such folders is the generic one until that package's build writes its own; the create runs that build for genshin-world, a `scripts` devDependency, so its barrel ends exact.

The barrel is one `export * from` line per module under `src`, sorted, each keeping its `.ts` extension — which node's own resolution requires of a relative import and a bundler takes as it is — leaving out the tests (`NON_SOURCE_SUFFIXES`), ambient `.d.ts` files, every module under `src/internal/`, and any module with no export — a CLI or a test setup is a program, and listing it would run it on every import of the package. Whether a module exports is read from rolldown's own oxc parse (`parseSync`'s `staticExports`, which counts a type-only export), so no TypeScript program is loaded and a package's barrel costs milliseconds. The `"vue"` answer first writes `src/components/index.ts`, one `export { default as <Name> }` per `.vue` file, which the source barrel then lists like any other module. A component is named by its path as Nuxt names the app's (`getComponentName`): its PascalCase folders and file joined, a folder's `Index.vue` by the folder, and a leading part the file already starts with dropped, so `Login/Screen/Index.vue` exports `LoginScreen` and a package lays its components out exactly as the app does, each in a folder beside its fixture, tests and images.

## Internal modules are private

- **Settled — a hand-written `src/index.ts` as a package's curated public surface.** The barrel lists every module under `src` outside `src/internal/` and never one under it, so a package keeps a module private by moving it into that folder, subfolders kept, and its imports follow (`#src/internal/…`). The owner's reason: "we always just have auto things, we don't have to care about what we expose". A hand-written entry bought a `.gitignore` un-ignore, a precheck skip and a build-cache special case, and nothing the folder does not already give. `generateExports` leaves the folder out of every barrel, so the build and the precheck agree.

## The build keeps the module graph

The barrel is the entry, and the build writes one output file per module it reaches (`unbundle`), so `dist` mirrors `src` and the barrel stays the one `.` export. tsdown is rolldown underneath, and that option is rolldown's module-preserving output; it neither writes the barrel nor decides which modules are public, so the generator stays. The reason is the consumer's bundler: a bundler's unit is the file, so a package built into one `dist/index.js` keeps every top-level call in it (a drizzle table, a schema derived from one) once any export is imported, while one file per module lets `sideEffects` drop each module no import reaches. The alternatives lost on cost: a list of pure annotations is a roster to keep true, and a subpath per cheap part is the second entry `references/subpaths.md` refuses.

A package opts out when nothing prunes its output: the infrastructure program is run once and imported by nothing, so it sets `unbundle: false` in its own config. Four consequences follow. A vendored dependency's files are written under `vendor`, because `npm pack` never ships a folder named `node_modules`. A folder loses its leading dot (pnpm's `.pnpm`), because the tools that move a `dist` skip a hidden folder: CI's artifact upload dropped the vendored files, and the app build could not resolve them. That folder is named by the package and its version, and loses pnpm's peer suffix, which pnpm keeps whole on Linux and shortens to a hash on Windows: a declaration imports the vendored file by that path, so the suffix made the size record differ between CI and a Windows checkout. A Vue package keeps its stylesheets in one `style.css` (`css.splitting` off, its rules put in module-id order by `mergeStylesheetsPlugin`) and no module imports one, since Node loads a Vue package's `dist` in scripts and benchmarks and cannot load a `.css` file; the package answers `sideEffects` with the stylesheet glob so a bundler keeps the page's import of `style.css`. `unbundledBarrels.test.ts` fails a `dist` holding a hidden folder, a vendored folder with a peer suffix, or a module that imports a stylesheet. The bundle-size record rolls the modules of a package into one row per extension (`references/dist-size.md`).

What makes it work looks redundant until it is gone:

- **`entry` is stated even though it is tsdown's own default.** Left unset, tsdown checks that `src/index.ts` exists _while resolving the config_, before any hook runs — so a package whose barrel is not on disk dies with `No input files`, which is every fresh clone. A literal entry reaches rolldown, which reads it after `build:prepare`.
- **The generator runs from `packages/configuration`'s built `dist`, so that build must be current.** The order `generateExports` writes is the one perfectionist's `sort-exports` checks, case-insensitively. A checkout whose configuration build predates that order (a git worktree's, say) writes every package's barrel in the old order on its next build. Build the configuration package once there (`pnpm -C packages/configuration build`).

## A name exported twice is a type error, never a silent drop

Every line is `export *`, so two modules exporting the same name are an ambiguity TypeScript reports as `TS2308` — in the package's own typecheck, and in every consumer resolving its source. That is why the generator is ours and not ctix's: ctix resolved the same collision by dropping the name from the barrel with a warning and exit 0, so a rename could remove a public export with `publint`, `attw`, `deps.onlyImport` and typecheck all green. A module listed beside a hand-written barrel that re-exports it — `genshin-interface`'s `save` — is no collision, because both paths reach the same binding.

Generation is **unguarded** — it runs on every build. It reads as a function of the source file list, and a skip keyed on that list would save milliseconds while trusting a key to see every way the output can move; CI's task cache already replays `dist` and the barrels together, keyed on every file the build read.

**A new module reaches the barrel at the package's next build.** tsdown calls `build:prepare` inside its build pass, so a file added to `src` is absent from the barrel until that package is built again, and a sibling resolving the `source` arm reads a barrel that never learned about it. `pnpm dev` runs `vp run -w build:packages` before `nuxt dev` starts, and that task regenerates a barrel whenever its package's source changed. An edit inside an existing module — a new export included — needs nothing, since `export *` re-exports whatever the file holds.

## A subpath is a hand-written barrel

The generated barrel is the package's `.` entry and reaches every module but a subpath's. A subpath that must reach only part of the package — `genshin-interface`'s `save`, the save's own entry, which the app's server loads without the interface's components — is a hand-written file of `export * from` lines at `src/<entry>.ts` (or `src/<dir>/index.ts`), built as its own entry and named by an export arm whose `source` is that file.

The generated barrel leaves it out. `getSubpathExclusions` reads the manifest's exports map, and each arm's `source` says what to leave out: one at `src/<dir>/index.ts` leaves out the folder, and one at any other `src` file leaves out that module. The root arm and the manifest's own arm name no subpath, and an arm whose `source` lies outside `src` names no module of the barrel. A module no arm names stays in the root barrel, so an entry loaded by path without an arm (a worker, a bin) keeps its module there as it always did. Nothing in a hook or a config lists those modules, so the root never re-exports what a subpath reaches. A consumer importing such a name from the root moves to the subpath: `genshin-interface`'s `constants` and `getFixtureImageName` left the root that way, `genshin-world`'s components import them from `genshin-interface/constants`, and `@esposter/configuration`'s `constants` arm moved its four root importers to `@esposter/configuration/constants`. The precheck derives the same list from the same manifest with the same function, so `ai:precheck` compares a barrel without those lines too.

## Why the packages are not built more concurrently

The wall time is one topological chain, because a sibling's `source` arm points at its generated — and gitignored — barrel, so a worker count past what the graph allows changes nothing. What already answers the dev loop is vp's task cache, which restores an unchanged package's `dist` and rebuilds only what changed, and CI replays the whole set when nothing it read has changed.
